title: Authentication and authorisation on data platforms

videos.script: A pharmacy keeps a list of its customers. Names, addresses, and the medicines each of them buys. {{table}} Somebody connects to that database. Two questions decide what happens next. Who are you? And what may you see? {{gates}} The first is answered once, at the door, by a password, a certificate or the operating system. The second is asked again on every statement. {{every}} Get the first wrong and the grants are checked against a name anybody can claim. Get the second wrong and everybody who logs in can read everything. {{wrong}} This lesson is the door. One login per person and one per program. A password the server never sees. A file that decides how each name is proved. And a log of who came in. {{door}} By the end, everybody can connect, and nobody can read a single row. Lesson 2 decides what each of them may have. {{end}}
